library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250801)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("ParraGuillen_2025_v937"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("ParraGuillen_2025_v937"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-025-01546-9>

V937 is a bioselected Coxsackievirus A21 given intratumorally (i.t.) or
intravenously (i.v.) to patients with advanced solid tumours. Parra-Guillen
and colleagues pooled serum V937 RNA and neutralising anti-V937 antibody (ADA)
titres from four trials and built a semi-mechanistic PK-ADA model in NONMEM
(Fig. 1; the NONMEM code is in ESM 2):

* **Viral kinetics** -- three compartments: serum (`central`, volume VS), a
  theoretical tumour compartment (`peripheral1`, VTUM) and other tissues
  (`peripheral2`, VPER). Both peripheral compartments share one
  intercompartmental clearance (QTUM = QPER). An i.t. dose is placed in the
  tumour compartment, and only the fraction FIT of it is available for
  distribution to serum.
* **ADA dynamics** -- serum virus activates B-cell synthesis through a
  saturable term `KSYN * C / (C + EC50)`. Three B-cell states in series
  (`bcell1` to `bcell3`, transit rate KTR) delay the appearance of circulating
  ADA (`ada`), which is degraded first-order (KDEG). ADA has no effect on viral
  clearance, which was the paper's main finding.
* **Pre-existing ADA** -- about 10% of patients had ADA before treatment. The
  observed baseline titre, when it is at or above the 1:16 detection limit,
  is added to the model-predicted ADA (column `ADA_TITER_BASE`).

The paper goes on to graft the ADA model onto the authors' earlier
physiologically based V937 tumour-response framework (Parra-Guillen 2023,
Clin Pharmacol Ther 114:623-632) for an in-silico neutralisation exercise
(Fig. 3; ESM 4). That framework's viral, tumour and immune parameters are
published in the 2023 paper, not in this one, so the tumour-response layer is
not part of this model.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("ParraGuillen_2025_v937"))$population
str(pop[c("n_subjects", "n_studies", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct")])
```

208 adults with advanced solid tumours from four Merck Sharp & Dohme trials
(Table 1): V937-006 (i.t. monotherapy, melanoma, n = 70), V937-007 (i.t. with
pembrolizumab, melanoma, n = 35), MK3475-200 Part A (i.v. monotherapy, n = 18)
and Part B (i.v. with pembrolizumab, non-small cell lung or bladder cancer,
n = 85). Mean age 65.3 years, mean weight 84.6 kg, 30.3% female, 92.8% White.
The analysis used 3628 serum V937 RNA levels (44% below the 3000 copies/mL
detection limit) and 2163 ADA titres (33% below the 1:16 limit; ESM 6 Table
S2).

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| VS (`lvc`) | 87.9 L | Table 2; ESM 2 THETA(2) |
| CL (`lcl`) | 111 L/h, IIV 67.5% CV | Table 2; ESM 2 THETA(3), $OMEGA 0.375 FIX |
| QTUM = QPER (`lq`) | 35.3 L/h | Table 2; ESM 2 THETA(4) and `Q3 = Q` |
| VTUM (`lvp`) | 103 L | Table 2; ESM 2 THETA(5) |
| VPER (`lvp2`) | 893 L | Table 2; ESM 2 THETA(7) |
| FIT (`logitfdepot`) | 0.201, logit-scale IIV variance 4.17 | Table 2 (footnote b); ESM 2 THETA(8), $OMEGA 4.17 FIX |
| PK residual error (`expSd`) | 1.33 log(copies/mL) | Table 2; ESM 2 THETA(1) |
| KSYN (`lksyn`) | 113 DF/h, IIV 395% CV | Table 2 |
| EC50 (`lec50`) | 0.754 x 10^8 copies/L | Table 2; ESM 2 `TVEC50 = THETA(12)*1e8` |
| Hill coefficient (`hill`) | 1 (fixed) | ESM 2 THETA(13) `GA = 1 FIX` |
| KTR (`lktr`) | 5.14 x 10^-3 1/h, IIV 95.2% CV | Table 2 |
| KDEG (`lkdeg`) | 0.250 x 10^-3 1/h, IIV 96.8% CV | Table 2 |
| ADA residual error (`expSd_ada_total`) | 1.01 log(DF) | Table 2 |
| Three-compartment viral ODEs | -- | Fig. 1; ESM 2 $DES `DADT(1)`, `DADT(2)`, `DADT(4)` |
| B-cell chain and ADA ODEs | -- | Fig. 1; ESM 2 $DES `DADT(3)`, `DADT(5)` to `DADT(7)` |
| i.t. bioavailability on the tumour compartment | -- | ESM 2 `F2` with logit IIV |
| Pre-existing ADA offset | added when `NAB0 >= 16` | Results (PK-ADA Model); ESM 2 $PK `BASENAB`, $ERROR `IPRED` |
| Log-scale observations with 0.001 offset | -- | ESM 2 $ERROR `LOG(F+0.001)`, `LOG(NAB+0.001+BASENAB)` |

# Dose units

The model is in viral RNA **copies**: the observations are copies/mL
(the ESM 2 scale factor `S1 = V1*1000` converts copies/L to copies/mL) and
EC50 is in copies/L. The trials dosed in TCID50, and the paper does not print
the TCID50-to-copies factor used to build the NONMEM dataset. This vignette
uses **1500 copies per TCID50**, the `RATIO = 1500 ; virions/TCID50` constant
in the same authors' tumour-response code (ESM 4), where the ADA model's EC50
(copies/L) is applied directly to serum virions/L. With this factor, the
simulated serum levels fall in the range of the observed data in Fig. 2A
(below); without it (1 copy per TCID50) a 1 x 10^9 TCID50 i.v. dose would
peak near 10^4 copies/mL, about 3 logs below the earliest observations.

```{r dose-units}
copies_per_tcid50 <- 1500
```

# Structural checks

```{r structural}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("ParraGuillen_2025_v937"))
th <- mod$theta

# The Discussion reports a mean transit time of 24.3 days for ADA appearance.
# Three B-cell states, each left at rate KTR, give MTT = 3 / KTR.
mtt_days <- 3 / exp(th[["lktr"]]) / 24
# The Discussion reports a large volume of distribution (> 1000 L).
vss <- exp(th[["lvc"]]) + exp(th[["lvp"]]) + exp(th[["lvp2"]])
# EC50 in copies/mL (the paper's text quotes 7.54 x 10^7 'copies/mL', which
# is the Table 2 value in copies/L).
ec50_per_ml <- exp(th[["lec50"]]) / 1000

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Check = c("Mean transit time of ADA appearance (days)", "Vss = VS + VTUM + VPER (L)",
              "Typical FIT", "EC50 (copies/mL)"),
    Model = c(sprintf("%.2f", mtt_days), sprintf("%.0f", vss),
              sprintf("%.3f", plogis(th[["logitfdepot"]])), sprintf("%.3g", ec50_per_ml)),
    Paper = c("24.3 (Discussion)", "> 1000 (Discussion)", "0.201 (Table 2)", "7.54 x 10^4 (Table 2, converted)")
  )
)

stopifnot(
  abs(mtt_days - 24.3) < 0.05,
  vss > 1000,
  abs(plogis(th[["logitfdepot"]]) - 0.201) < 1e-9,
  identical(mod$state, c("central", "peripheral1", "peripheral2", "bcell1", "bcell2", "bcell3", "ada"))
)
```

# Virtual cohort

Four arms follow the dosing schedules of ESM 5 Table S1: i.t. 3 x 10^8 TCID50
on days 1, 3, 5 and 8 then on day 1 of each 21-day cycle (V937-006), and i.v.
1, 3 or 10 x 10^8 TCID50 as 30-min infusions on days 1, 3 and 5 then on day 1
of each 21-day cycle (MK3475-200 Part A). Dosing runs for about one year.
Pembrolizumab has no effect in the final model, so the combination arms are
not simulated separately. All simulated subjects are ADA-naive at baseline
(`ADA_TITER_BASE = 0`); pre-existing ADA is examined separately below.

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 100

make_arm <- function(arm, route, tcid50, n, id_offset) {
  dose_days <- if (route == "i.t.") c(0, 2, 4, 7) else c(0, 2, 4)
  dose_days <- c(dose_days, seq(21, 357, by = 21))
  obs_h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.25), seq(48, 700 * 24, by = 24))))
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  doses <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = dose_days * 24) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = tcid50 * copies_per_tcid50,
           cmt = if (route == "i.t.") "peripheral1" else "central",
           dur = if (route == "i.t.") 0 else 0.5, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_h) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dur = 0, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(arm = arm, ADA_TITER_BASE = 0) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- bind_rows(
  make_arm("i.t. 3e8 TCID50", "i.t.", 3e8, n_per_arm, 0L),
  make_arm("i.v. 1e8 TCID50", "i.v.", 1e8, n_per_arm, 100L),
  make_arm("i.v. 3e8 TCID50", "i.v.", 3e8, n_per_arm, 200L),
  make_arm("i.v. 1e9 TCID50", "i.v.", 1e9, n_per_arm, 300L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame",
                       useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  filter(!duplicated(paste(id, time)))
# Residual error drawn explicitly on the log scale (Data Analysis: additive
# error in the log domain for each endpoint).
th_sd <- mod$theta
sim <- sim |>
  mutate(
    Cc_obs = Cc * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, th_sd[["expSd"]])),
    ada_obs = ada_total * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, th_sd[["expSd_ada_total"]])),
    day = time / 24
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

## Serum V937 after the first dose (Fig. 2A)

```{r fig2a, fig.cap = "Serum V937 over the first 48 h (before the second dose): median and 5th-95th percentiles of simulated observations by arm; dashed line = 3000 copies/mL detection limit. Compare Figure 2A of Parra-Guillen 2025."}
first_dose <- sim |>
  filter(time >= 0.25, time <= 47.75) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc_obs), lo = quantile(Cc_obs, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc_obs, 0.95),
            pct_bld = 100 * mean(Cc_obs < 3000), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(first_dose, aes(time / 24, med, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3000, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (days)", y = "V937 RNA (copies/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure 2A pools all arms and is prediction-corrected, so the comparison is
visual. The observed data sit between about 10^4 and 10^7 copies/mL in the
first hours after dosing, and the fraction below the detection limit climbs
from near zero at about 0.1 day to roughly 45% at about 2 days and 100% beyond
a week. The simulated pooled percentage below the limit follows the same
course:

```{r fig2a-bld}
bld <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% c(2.5, 24, 47.75)) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(`% below 3000 copies/mL` = round(100 * mean(Cc_obs < 3000), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  rename(`Time after first dose (h)` = time)
knitr::kable(bld)
```

## ADA over time (Fig. 2B)

```{r fig2b, fig.cap = "Neutralising ADA titre (dilution factor): median and 5th-95th percentiles of simulated observations by arm; dotted line = 1:16 detection limit. Compare Figure 2B of Parra-Guillen 2025."}
ada_sum <- sim |>
  filter(time %% 24 == 0) |>
  group_by(arm, day) |>
  summarise(med = median(ada_obs), lo = quantile(ada_obs, 0.05), hi = quantile(ada_obs, 0.95),
            pct_bld = 100 * mean(ada_obs < 16), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(ada_sum, aes(day, med, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 16, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "ADA (1/DL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

In Figure 2B the observed median ADA rises within the first month to between
roughly 10^3 and 10^4 and stays there, with fewer than about 10% of samples
below the 1:16 limit after the first month. The simulated pooled cohort is
checked against that plateau and that rise:

```{r fig2b-check}
pooled <- sim |>
  filter(time %% 24 == 0, day %in% c(0, 7, 30, 100, 200, 300)) |>
  group_by(day) |>
  summarise(median_ada = signif(median(ada_obs), 3),
            pct_below_16 = round(100 * mean(ada_obs < 16), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(pooled |> rename(`Day` = day, `Median ADA (DF)` = median_ada,
                              `% below 1:16` = pct_below_16))

plateau <- pooled |> filter(day %in% c(100, 200, 300))
stopifnot(
  # Before dosing every naive subject sits at the 0.001 offset.
  pooled$pct_below_16[pooled$day == 0] == 100,
  # Plateau median within the 10^3 - 10^4 band of Fig. 2B (a factor of 3
  # either side for the prediction correction and the arm mix).
  all(plateau$median_ada > 300),
  all(plateau$median_ada < 3e4),
  # Fewer than a fifth of samples below the limit once ADA is established.
  all(plateau$pct_below_16 < 20)
)
```

## Pre-existing ADA

The paper adds an individual's observed baseline titre to the predicted ADA
when it is at or above 1:16, and ignores values below that limit. With the
same individual parameters the three scenarios therefore differ by exactly the
offset:

```{r baseline-ada}
base_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(c(0, 8, 64), function(b) {
  make_arm(paste("ADA_TITER_BASE =", b), "i.v.", 3e8, 1, 0L) |>
    mutate(ADA_TITER_BASE = b, id = match(b, c(0, 8, 64)))
}))
base_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), base_ev, keep = "ADA_TITER_BASE",
                            returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  filter(!duplicated(paste(id, time)))
offset <- base_sim |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(d8 = ada_total[ADA_TITER_BASE == 8] - ada_total[ADA_TITER_BASE == 0],
            d64 = ada_total[ADA_TITER_BASE == 64] - ada_total[ADA_TITER_BASE == 0],
            .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(max(abs(offset$d8)) < 1e-6, max(abs(offset$d64 - 64)) < 1e-6)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Scenario = c("ADA_TITER_BASE = 8 (below 1:16)", "ADA_TITER_BASE = 64"),
                        `Added to predicted ADA` = c(max(abs(offset$d8)), mean(offset$d64)),
                        check.names = FALSE))
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA, so the check is internal: after a single dose,
AUC0-inf must equal `F * Dose / CL` for each subject (`F = 1` i.v.,
`F = FIT` i.t.). A single dose with a 7-day window is simulated per arm.

```{r pknca}
sd_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c("i.t.", "i.v.", "i.v.", "i.v.")), function(k) {
  route <- c("i.t.", "i.v.", "i.v.", "i.v.")[k]
  tcid <- c(3e8, 1e8, 3e8, 1e9)[k]
  ids <- (k - 1L) * 100L + seq_len(100)
  obs_h <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168)))
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = tcid * copies_per_tcid50,
               cmt = if (route == "i.t.") "peripheral1" else "central",
               dur = if (route == "i.t.") 0 else 0.5, dvid = NA_integer_),
    expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_h) |>
      mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dur = 0, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(route, format(tcid, scientific = TRUE), "TCID50"), ADA_TITER_BASE = 0)
})) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sd_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, sd_events, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame",
                          useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  filter(!duplicated(paste(id, time)))

sim_nca <- sd_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(sim_nca, sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- sd_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
knitr::kable(nca_tab |> rename(`Treatment` = treatment, `Cmax (copies/mL)` = cmax,
                               `Tmax (h)` = tmax, `AUC0-inf (copies*h/mL)` = aucinf.obs,
                               `t1/2 (h)` = half.life),
             caption = "Median single-dose NCA of the simulated cohort (no published NCA to compare).")

# Closed-form AUC per subject: F * Dose / CL, converted from copies*h/L to
# copies*h/mL.
indiv <- sd_sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cl = first(cl), fit = first(fit), .groups = "drop")
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(indiv, by = "id") |>
  left_join(dose_df |> select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  mutate(f = ifelse(grepl("^i.t.", treatment), fit, 1),
         auc_ref = f * amt / cl / 1000,
         pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES - auc_ref) / auc_ref)
knitr::kable(auc_chk |> group_by(treatment) |>
               summarise(`Median % difference, PKNCA vs F*Dose/CL` = round(median(pct_diff), 2),
                         .groups = "drop") |>
               rename(`Treatment` = treatment))
stopifnot(abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 5, quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 15)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **TCID50-to-copies factor.** The paper does not state the factor used to
  convert TCID50 doses into the RNA-copy dose units of the model. Simulations
  here use 1500 copies per TCID50, the virions-per-TCID50 ratio in the
  authors' tumour-response code (ESM 4). Users with the factor from the
  original dataset should substitute it; the model itself takes doses in
  copies.
* **EC50 units.** Table 2 gives EC50 = 0.754 x 10^8 copies/L, and ESM 2 applies
  it to `A(1)/V1` (copies/L). The Results text quotes "7.54 x 10^7 copies/mL";
  the table and code agree, so the model uses copies/L (7.54 x 10^4
  copies/mL).
* **IIV of FIT.** Table 2 lists 4.17 for the IIV of the logit-transformed FIT
  with a footnote describing a CV% formula. ESM 2, which fixes every other PK
  value at its Table 2 estimate, sets `$OMEGA 4.17 FIX` for this term, so
  4.17 is used as the logit-scale variance. The other IIV terms are CV%
  values converted with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, the inverse of the
  paper's `CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`; this reproduces the ESM 2 CL value
  (0.375) exactly.
* **Zero-concentration guard.** ESM 2 sets serum concentrations below 10^-6
  copies/L to zero before computing the B-cell drive. This is a numerical
  guard with no effect on the drive (it is 10^14 times below EC50) and is not
  reproduced.
* **0.001 offset.** The ESM 2 predictions carry `+ 0.001` inside the log for
  both endpoints, so `Cc` and `ada_total` include it. It is 6 orders of
  magnitude below the V937 detection limit and 4 below the ADA detection limit.
* **Censoring.** Observations below the detection limits were handled by the
  M3 likelihood during estimation. That is part of fitting, not of the model,
  and is not encoded.
* **Pre-existing ADA.** The paper reports that 20 patients (about 10%) had
  ADA above 1:16 at baseline but not the distribution of their titres, so the
  simulated cohort is ADA-naive; the offset behaviour is shown separately.
* **Covariates.** Route, combination with pembrolizumab and pre-existing ADA
  were screened on KSYN, KTR and KDEG (ESM 3) and none was retained.
* **Tumour-response layer.** The in-silico neutralisation exercise (Fig. 3,
  ESM 4) couples this ADA model to the Parra-Guillen 2023 physiologically
  based V937 framework, whose viral-dynamic, tumour and immune parameters are
  not printed in this paper. It is not included here.
